objective: Attempt to make ECDAT fail using hostile scan inputs for defensive validation and record attack input, affected component, impact, mitigation, and permanent regression test.

scenarios.name: Zip Slip Archive Directory Traversal Attack

attack_input.payload_description: Crafted ZIP archive containing relative path traversal entries (e.g. '../../etc/cron.d/evil' and '..\..\windows\system32\calc.exe') and null byte terminations.
adversarial_properties: Null byte injection in entry name (evil.sh\0.txt)

impact.failure_mode: Arbitrary File Overwrite & Remote Code Execution
impact.risk_description: If unmitigated, extraction of hostile archives allows writing outside the sandboxed extraction root, overwriting critical binaries, configurations, or system cron jobs.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Pre-extraction canonical path containment check using Path.resolve() and strict root boundary validation with null-byte rejection.
architectural_invariants: Zero extraction outside isolated temporary destination folder
PathTraversalError raised deterministically before file handle creation
Immediate abort on null byte in member name

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts PathTraversalError is raised and zero bytes are written outside target extract directory.

scenarios.name: Decompression Bomb / Zip Bomb Denial of Service

attack_input.payload_description: Highly compressed zip bomb containing repeating zeroes with a compression ratio exceeding 1000:1 (e.g. 10 KB file expanding to > 50 GB).

impact.risk_description: Decompression bombs rapidly exhaust available disk space and virtual memory, causing host kernel panic or denial of service to the scanning worker.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Strict pre-read ratio calculation, individual member size limits (25MB), total uncompressed byte limits (100MB), and file count caps (1,000 files).
architectural_invariants: Max compression ratio capped at 100.0:1
Max uncompressed bytes strictly clamped to 100 MB
DecompressionBombError raised prior to disk allocation

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts DecompressionBombError is raised when compression ratio or uncompressed size limits are exceeded.

scenarios.name: Billion Laughs XML Entity Expansion Bomb in CBOM/SBOM

attack_input.payload_description: CycloneDX XML document containing recursive exponential entity declarations (lol1 expands to 10 lol, lol2 to 10 lol1, ..., lol9 to 10 lol8) generating gigabytes in memory.

impact.failure_mode: Parser Crash / Memory Blowup / Server Hang
impact.risk_description: Unrestricted XML entity parsing triggers uncontrolled memory growth leading to process termination (OOM kill) and potential local file disclosure via XXE.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Strict enforcement of defusedxml library with DTD entity resolution and external entity loading disabled at the parser layer.
architectural_invariants: Standard xml.dom.minidom and xml.etree.ElementTree are completely forbidden
Entity expansion raises DefusedXmlException and aborts safely
External network/file entity loading is permanently disabled

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts defusedxml catches entity expansion and raises DefusedXmlException without memory growth.

attack_input.payload_description: Crafted source code containing long repeating strings with trailing non-matching characters (e.g. 50,000 characters of 'a' followed by '!') designed to trigger polynomial or exponential backtracking.

impact.risk_description: Catastrophic regex backtracking monopolizes 100% CPU on worker threads, causing scan timeouts and stalling scanner pipelines.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Pre-line length truncation (MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 10,000 chars), non-backtracking regex compilation, and bounded match timeouts.
architectural_invariants: Lines longer than MAX_LINE_LENGTH are truncated or segmented before regex scanning
Regex execution time is bounded and deterministic (< 100ms)
Non-backtracking atomic groups and possessive patterns applied

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts regex evaluation of 50,000-char repeating adversarial string completes in under 50ms.

scenarios.name: Deeply Nested CBOM/SBOM Recursion Bomb (>64 levels)

attack_input.payload_description: JSON CBOM payload with 100+ levels of recursively nested sub-components designed to exhaust call stack limits during deserialization or traversal.
adversarial_properties: Recursive object nesting beyond call stack frames (> 64 levels)
Deeply nested arrays of cryptographic dependencies

impact.risk_description: Recursive tree traversal without recursion depth limits crashes Node.js with 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded'.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Iterative stack traversal with strict MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 64 check and visited reference tracking.
architectural_invariants: Nesting depth strictly capped at 64 levels
Depth violations return structured error response without crashing
Cycle detection prevents infinite loop traversal

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts validateCbomStructure detects 70-level object and returns validation error containing 'exceeds 64 levels'.

scenarios.name: Embedded Private Key Trap in Public Certificate Files

attack_input.payload_description: Public certificate file containing embedded RSA/EC/ED25519 private key blocks (-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----) concatenated into certificate fields or diagnostic extensions.
adversarial_properties: Embedded private key block in cert bundle
Encrypted private key concatenated with public cert
Hostile attempt to make scanner ingest or display private key material

impact.failure_mode: Private Key Ingestion & Leakage in Inventory/BOM
impact.risk_description: Ingesting private keys into CBOM inventory leads to secret persistence, report exposure, and violation of the zero-secret invariant.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Pre-parse private key detection, immediate zeroization, stripping of private key blocks, and logging of security warnings.
architectural_invariants: Private key blocks are never stored in CBOM certificates
Detection triggers sanitization without crashing the scanner
Scanner inventories only public metadata (subject, issuer, algorithm, key size)

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts certificate parser scrubs private key block and does not include it in certificate inventory.

scenarios.name: Truncated & Malformed ASN.1 DER Certificate Payload

attack_input.payload_description: Truncated X.509 DER byte stream with invalid ASN.1 length headers (e.g. declared length 0xFFFF with 10 bytes payload) designed to trigger parser buffer overreads.

impact.risk_description: Malformed ASN.1 structures can crash unhardened parsers or abort scanner pipelines unexpectedly.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Defensive try-except wrapper around pyca/cryptography x509 loader returning structured error diagnostic without scanner abort.
architectural_invariants: Malformed certificates are recorded as scan errors with non-fatal status
Buffer boundaries strictly checked before slicing bytes
No unhandled exceptions bubble up to CI runner

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts parse_der_bytes gracefully returns parsing error without crashing.

scenarios.name: Deeply Encapsulated PCAP Packet Loop / Recursion Attack

attack_input.payload_description: Crafted PCAP capture file containing packets with 100+ nested tunnel encapsulations (e.g. GRE inside IP inside GRE inside IP...) or malformed header length fields.

impact.risk_description: Deep packet parsing loops lead to Python RecursionError or unbounded CPU consumption processing fake tunnels.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Hard limit on packet encapsulation depth (MAX_ENCAPSULATION_DEPTH = 8) and strict per-packet memory bounds.
architectural_invariants: Layer parsing terminates at depth 8 with safe warning
Malformed lengths drop the packet and continue scanning
Zero memory allocation based on untrusted packet length headers

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts SafePcapParser caps layer parsing at max depth and processes remaining packets safely.

attack_input.payload_description: Single-line JavaScript/Python file with 500,000 characters without newlines, packing thousands of concatenated crypto calls and strings.
adversarial_properties: Gigantic single-line length (500 KB on 1 line)
Multiple regex matches on single line

impact.failure_mode: Evidence Buffer Bloat & Line Splitter OOM
impact.risk_description: Extracting evidence snippets from 500,000-character lines bloats CBOM findings and report sizes into megabytes per finding.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: MAX_EVIDENCE_LENGTH clamp (200 characters) and line truncation before regex scanning.
architectural_invariants: Evidence snippets are strictly clamped to MAX_EVIDENCE_LENGTH
Line processing memory is bounded by character limits
Findings contain clean truncated evidence markers

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts findings on 500,000-character line clamp evidence snippets to <= 200 characters.

attack_input.payload_description: Directory structure containing circular symbolic links (e.g. link_a -> link_b -> link_a and parent_dir/loop -> parent_dir) designed to induce infinite traversal loops.

impact.risk_description: Scanner follows circular symlinks indefinitely until disk recursion limit or process memory exhausts.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Visited realpath / inode tracking and strict exclusion of unresolved symlinks pointing outside scan root.
architectural_invariants: Every directory realpath is tracked in a visited set
Symlinks are never traversed circularly
Links escaping the root directory are automatically pruned

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts FileDiscovery terminates cleanly in visited circular directories without infinite looping.

attack_input.payload_description: Binary file starting with valid ELF magic bytes (\x7fELF) but followed by corrupted section headers, negative table offsets, and truncated string tables.
adversarial_properties: Valid magic bytes with corrupted section offsets

impact.failure_mode: Unhandled Struct Unpack Error / Parser Crash
impact.risk_description: Corrupted binary headers cause unhandled struct.error or EOFError, failing container and binary analysis pipelines.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Pre-validation of section header bounds, safe struct unpack guards, and non-fatal corruption reporting.
architectural_invariants: Binary parsing operates within bounded memory buffers
Invalid headers return structured parsing error and continue
Zero unhandled unpack exceptions in binary scanner

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts binary analyzer catches corrupted ELF header and returns graceful error status without crash.

scenarios.name: Circular Dependency Graph Explosion in SBOM / Manifests

attack_input.payload_description: Package manifest (e.g. package.json or pom.xml) defining circular cyclic dependency chains (pkg-A -> pkg-B -> pkg-C -> pkg-A).

impact.failure_mode: Infinite Loop & Stack Overflow during Graph Traversal
impact.risk_description: Traversing dependency graphs without cycle detection causes infinite loops during transitive vulnerability propagation.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Cycle detection using visited set during graph walk and depth-bounded transitive resolution.
architectural_invariants: Visited package IDs tracked along resolution path
Detected cycles flagged and pruned from traversal
Dependency depth strictly capped at maximum 30 levels

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts dependency graph resolver prunes circular package references without hanging.

scenarios.name: Canary Token & Secret Bait in Code Diagnostics

attack_input.input_type: Hostile Source Code with Secret Bait
attack_input.payload_description: Source code repository containing deliberate canary tokens, AWS API keys, and fake passwords designed to be echoed into error traces or scan diagnostics.
adversarial_properties: Embedded canary tokens in comments and code
High-entropy secret strings triggering error handlers
Hostile exception messages containing auth tokens

impact.failure_mode: Secret Exfiltration via CI Logs / Diagnostics
impact.risk_description: Echoing untrusted code snippets directly into unredacted CI build logs can expose credentials or canary trigger alerts.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Automated regex redaction of canary tokens, API keys, and PEM blocks before writing to logs, SARIF, or reports.
architectural_invariants: Zero unredacted canary tokens or private keys in diagnostic output
Redacted values replaced with cryptographic hash fingerprints [REDACTED_CANARY SHA256:8chars]
Sanitization applied to both stdout/stderr and serialized JSON reports

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts redact_secrets scrubs canary tokens and private keys from diagnostic logs.

scenarios.name: Hostile Broken AST Remediation Patch Injection

attack_input.payload_description: Malformed Python source code designed to confuse the AST patch generator (e.g. unclosed parentheses, mixed tabs/spaces, invalid indentation).
adversarial_properties: Malformed Python syntax in patch target

impact.failure_mode: Generation of Malformed Patches / Broken Build
impact.risk_description: Generating patches on invalid syntax could corrupt source files or introduce syntax errors into target repositories.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Pre-generation syntax parsing and post-generation syntax validation lifecycle rejecting any invalid transformation.
architectural_invariants: Patches are validated using ast.parse() before generation
Syntax validation failure blocks patch emission with clean error
Zero unverified patches applied to disk

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts SafePatchGenerator and validate_syntax reject malformed syntax and return valid: False.

scenarios.name: Silent Crash / Non-Zero Exit Code Masking in CI

attack_input.payload_description: Corrupted configuration or simulated catastrophic scanner failure designed to test whether the CI scanner pipeline accurately preserves non-zero exit codes.
adversarial_properties: Hostile attempt to bypass release gate via exit code 0

impact.failure_mode: Silent Failure / False Positive Release Approval
impact.risk_description: If a scanner crash is masked or swallowed with exit code 0, broken or compromised code will pass release gates undetected.

mitigation.defensive_strategy: Deterministic exit code preservation and Gate 5 silent crash interception (exit code 2 on internal crash).
architectural_invariants: Scanner crashes NEVER exit with 0
Internal runner errors exit with code 2
Release gate strictly fails if scanner encounters unhandled fatal exception

regression_test.deterministic_assertion: Asserts scanner crash is never conflated with clean pass (exit code 2 strictly distinct from 0).
